description: Extract pages from a PDF. RANGE LANGUAGE: "3" is a page, "1-5" a range, "7-" to the end, "-4" from the start, "last" the last page; "1,1" legitimately means two copies. Errors are numbered PDFR-* findings that name the real problem — a backwards range comes back with the swap suggestion, out-of-bounds names the document's true page count. Empty `pages` selects all. THE FILE IS DIAGNOSED FIRST (same PDFI-* structure checks as merge_pdfs); encrypted or truncated files are refused with the diagnosis, not a parser stack trace. MODES: "extract" writes one PDF with the selected pages to `out`; "each" writes one PDF per selected page into `outDir` (named <base>-p<N>.pdf, never overwriting). Returns { summary{sourcePages,selected,outputs}, inspection, findings[], wrote }.

out.description: extract mode: absolute path of the output PDF.

outDir.description: each mode: absolute directory for the per-page PDFs.

pages.description: Page selection, e.g. "1-3,5,9-" or "last". Empty = all pages.

path.description: Absolute path of the source PDF.

name: split_pdf
title: Split a PDF / extract pages — range language with real errors
